## Where the agents sat on the DRC model

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- On [BVDOutbreakSize][bvd] agents wrote the code. The judgements
  stayed with people
- They do best with something to check against. A simulation with known
  parameters, an analytic case, another group's estimate
- 333 of 425 pull requests, the unit of change on GitHub, came from my
  bot account

::: {.attribution}
[github.com/epiforecasts/BVDOutbreakSize][bvd], `README.md` · pull
request count from the GitHub API, 2026-09-11
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/exchange-workflow-split.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The nine workflow stages as a column of numbered boxes. To
the left, in brick, what stayed with people: choosing the question at
stage 1, which model at stage 2, what the genetic lower bound means at
stage 4, whether ascertainment holds at stage 8, which streams to trust
at stage 9. To the right, in teal, what agents did: reading French PDF
sitreps at stage 3, digitising the onset curve at stage 4, fitting
pipeline, releases and docs at stage 7, tests and recovery checks at
stage 8, sensitivity analyses and figures at stage 9."}

::: {.attribution}
Drawn for this talk, `scripts/exchange-workflow-split.py`, from the
[BVDOutbreakSize][bvd] `README.md` and `data/README.md`
:::
:::

## Agents building and checking the parts

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
- Bundibugyo virus disease, DRC. McCabe et al. replicated the day after
  their report, then a joint model across suspected, confirmed, deaths,
  exports and bed occupancy
- Agents read the French PDF situation reports. Two blind reads per
  vintage of the onset chart
- SitRep 087 changed the y axis steps from 20 to 25. Caught only by the
  reporting-triangle invariant
- Could agents build and check the simulators you learn against?

::: {.attribution}
[BVDOutbreakSize][bvd] `README.md` and `data/README.md`, SitReps 104 to
114 · McCabe et al. report of 18 May 2026
:::
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
![](../figures/exchange-bvd-outbreak-streams.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Posterior densities for the cumulative size of the outbreak,
one per data stream and one joint, with the confirmed-case stream far
to the right of the others."}

::: {.attribution}
Outbreak size by data stream, then jointly. June 2026 fit; the live
report is at
[epiforecasts.io/BVDOutbreakSize/stable](https://epiforecasts.io/BVDOutbreakSize/stable/)
:::
:::

## Agents that search over models

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Google's 2025/26 entry to the CDC hubs was an LLM-guided tree search
  over forecasting models. It topped influenza, COVID-19 and RSV,
  prospectively
- Bracher and Funk put the earlier 11% retrospective gain down to data
  revision leakage
- On the DRC model the search was by hand. Agents wrote each variant
  and the sensitivity analyses. We chose what to keep
- With composable parts the nodes are component swaps, and each part
  brings its own checks

::: {.attribution}
Martinson, Brenner, Plomecka, Williams, Reich and Shamsi 2026,
[arXiv:2605.16238](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16238) · Bracher and Funk
2026, [arXiv:2608.05883](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.05883) ·
[BVDOutbreakSize][bvd] `README.md`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/exchange-tree-search.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A tree. The root is a task, forecast admissions, scored on
held-out weeks. Four proposed models below it: ARIMA and a GAM in grey,
dropped, and two renewal models in teal, kept. Under the kept ones four
more variants, adding a reporting delay, a spline, day of week effects
and a wastewater stream, with the spline dropped. Arrows from the
survivors lead to a red box, an ensemble of the survivors is what gets
submitted. Side labels read propose, write the code, fit, score, expand
the best, many rounds."}

::: {.attribution}
Drawn for this talk, `scripts/exchange-schematics.py`
:::
